svg.title: Signals ask a process to stop.
svg.desc: A signal is a message to a running process. Ctrl-C sends an interrupt to the foreground job in the current terminal. A separate prominent kill -TERM PID example sends a termination request to a verified process owned by the reader. The diagram shows that request reaching the selected process and the result if it exits; a process can handle or ignore the request. Stopping a process does not remove its program file. Inspect ps first, never stop unknown processes, and beware loss of unsaved work.
svg.text: SIGNALS: ASK A PROCESS TO STOP.
A signal is a message to a running process, not a change to its file.
Ctrl-C sends an interrupt to this terminal's foreground job:
the command currently using the terminal, not every running process.
with a verified ID of YOUR process.
WARNING: stopping a process can lose unsaved work. Verify its identity first.
If it exits, that instance stops; the program file stays in place.
A process can handle or ignore this request. It is not a forced stop.
Inspect ps first. Never stop an unknown process.
